context: Module theory over a commutative unital ring
formulations: An A-module M is Noetherian if each submodule of M is finitely generated.
Equivalently, an A-module M is Noetherian if every ascending chain M_1⊆M_2⊆⋯ of its submodules eventually stabilizes.
Equivalently, an A-module M is Noetherian if every nonempty family of submodules contains an inclusion-maximal member.
review: ProofWiki defines all three equivalent conditions for modules over a commutative unital ring. The ideal-submodule identification for R as an R-module provides the exact eventual target for the separately screened Noetherian-ring module formulation. The word 'Noetherian' here is a property of a module over a specified base ring, not simply the Noetherian-ring predicate; circularity is avoided by defining submodules independently.

context: Topology of all subsets of a specified nonempty set (ProofWiki source convention)
formulations: For a nonempty set S, the discrete topology on S is P(S), the set of all subsets of S.
For a set S with the discrete topology, every singleton subset is open; conversely, if every singleton is open, then the topology is discrete.
review: The direct ProofWiki definition restricts its set S to nonempty. Its singleton-open condition is mathematically equivalent for arbitrary sets; for empty S the unique topology is discrete by the power-set construction. The eventual two-element discrete topology needed for the connectedness surjection criterion has nonempty S, so the source restriction poses no ambiguity in that application. A separate source with empty-set-inclusive convention should be sought before treating the general arbitrary-set extension as fully source-supported.
